about: Regression set for the CURRENT config.dashboards. Every scored answer below was established by opening the dashboard at its default state, screenshotting it, and reading the value by eye - not by trusting a model. Two questions are deliberately unscored; see their notes.
provenance: Ground truth read from clean default-state captures of each dashboard. These are third-party Tableau Public workbooks: if an author republishes with new data, these answers rot silently and a passing run means nothing. Re-verify against fresh captures before trusting a result, and update verified_on.
scoring: An entry is correct when every element of `expect` is satisfied by the final answer, case-insensitively. A string element must appear as a substring; an array element is satisfied if ANY of its strings appears (used for names with a common abbreviation).

questions.question: Which publisher has the highest total sales in the Top 5 Publishers chart?
questions.notes: The canonical 1-step reading demo. Large, clearly-labelled bars; if this fails, something is badly wrong.

questions.question: In the Top 10 Games by Sales chart, which single game has the highest global sales?
questions.notes: Unfiltered state. Note this is also the WRONG answer to vgs_ea_click - a stale, unfiltered frame produces exactly this string, which is how the settle-gate race was caught.

questions.question: Click the 'Electronic Arts' bar in the Top 5 Publishers chart to filter to that publisher, then report which single game has the highest global sales in the Top 10 Games chart
questions.notes: The load-bearing actuation test. The mark click applies a dashboard action filter that takes a 2.3-3.3s server round-trip; screenshot before it lands and the model reads the unfiltered chart and answers 'Wii Sports' with no error logged. Was 4/10 before the settle-gate fix, 10/10 after. If this regresses to Wii Sports, suspect the settle gate first.

questions.question: According to the Movies and TV Shows Distribution, what percentage of the Netflix catalog are Movies?
questions.notes: Value is printed inside the bubble (Movie 4,265 / 68.42%). Matches on 68.4 so a rounded 68.4% also passes.

questions.question: Which genre has the most titles in the Top 10 Genre chart, and how many titles does it have?
questions.notes: Two-part answer: needs both the label and the count, so it catches a model that reads the bar but not its data label.

questions.question: In the 'Cancellations by airport' chart, which airport has the most cancelled flights, and how many?
questions.notes: The axis label is truncated to 'John F. Kennedy..', so either the full name or JFK counts.

questions.question: What is the 'AVG Delay Time' value shown in the KPIs at the top of the dashboard?
questions.notes: Large KPI text. Tests plain figure-reading with no chart interpretation.

questions.question: In the 'Average Salary Trends (2020-2022)' chart, which experience level has the highest average salary?
questions.notes: Requires reading a multi-series line chart against its colour legend, not just a label.

questions.question: Use the Artists dropdown to select 'Ed Sheeran' and list the songs shown in the 'All songs by Artist' table.
questions.expected_answer: Castle on the Hill, Galway Girl, Perfect, Shape of You
questions.notes: Phrased as an interaction but is really a reading test: the dashboard already loads with Ed Sheeran selected, so no action is required. Kept because the four-item list catches partial reads.

questions.question: In the 'Number Of Songs By Artist' bubble chart, which artist appears to have the most songs?
questions.notes: UNSCORED. The bubble chart is too dense to establish truth even by careful manual inspection; only two bubbles carry labels. Both arms of the domain A/B answered 'Ed Sheeran', which is the value selected in the Artists dropdown rather than the largest bubble - i.e. plausibly wrong, but unprovable either way. Kept as a documented weak spot: this is one of config.dashboards' exampleQuestions and is a poor demo choice.

questions.question: In the 'Percent Remote Roles vs. Company Size' chart, scroll down to the Remote Ratio value of 100 and report which Company Size makes up the largest share of that pie.
questions.notes: Replaces the old unscored salaries_remote, which asked for a description and was unanswerable because the Remote Ratio 100 row sits below the fold with no scroll action. Now scorable: that pane has 222px of hidden content and one scroll step reveals the 100 row with its pie. Truth read by eye from a clean post-scroll capture - orange dominates that pie at ~55-60% against ~35% blue, and orange is M in the Company Size legend. The word form is REQUIRED, not stylistic: a bare "M" is scored as a case-insensitive SUBSTRING and would pass on almost any sentence, making the question always-green and worthless. PIXEL-MODE ONLY as a comparison: Remote Ratio is an API-operable filter, so api mode can reach 100 without scrolling (and answered 'L' when tried on 2026-08-10) - do not read this as an api-vs-pixel result.
